description: A crisp exterior entryway scene photographed in daylight. The facade is painted dark charcoal brick — a classic running-bond pattern with visible mortar joints in a contrasting lighter tone — giving the exterior a refined, northern-European character. The corner of the building is visible where two brick walls meet, creating an L-shaped backdrop. A white-painted exterior door with a traditional nine-pane divided-light window grid occupies the right side of the frame, its lower panel featuring applied vertical beadboard detailing. A white painted soffit lines the top of the frame. At the base of the composition, a lush planting of white hydrangea blooms in full flower spills forward, introducing a soft organic element against the hard brick. A gentle shadow falls across the brick wall beside the door, cast by the architecture above. The light is crisp midday or early afternoon exterior natural light. The palette is high-contrast dark gray brick, bright white trim and door, and pure white floral. Camera is at standing eye-level, roughly 5 feet, positioned in a three-quarter view showing the brick wall corner and the door in the same frame, at a normal focal length with a vignette-style composition that keeps the brick wall and door as the primary subjects.
